newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Loy Yang adds to diversity of Australia debt-ANZIB.
newsitem.headline: Loy Yang adds to diversity of Australia debt-ANZIB.

text.p: Loy Yang Power became the latest entry into this month's rush of non-government debt issuance on the Australian domestic market, offering A$300 million of inflation indexed bonds on Tuesday.
The 30-year bonds will be offered at a spread of 160 basis points over the Australian government's 2010 indexed bond through joint lead underwriters Macquarie Bank and ANZ Investment Bank (ANZIB).

"We think that is a very fair pricing. It should attract the interest of a broad diversity of investors with that sort of pricing," David Hornery, Head of Securities at ANZ Investment Bank told Reuters.

At current market levels it implies a real yield of some 6.3 percent, plus the rate of inflation, and compares with other infrastructure related bonds which are currently trading at around 130 basis points over.

Loy Yang Power is a consortium which was selected by the Victorian State government to buy the Loy Yang A Power Station and brown coal mine in Victoria's La Trobe Valley, and the issue would partially finance the A$4.9 billion purchase.
The offering is primarily targetted at domestic institutions although there has been a lot of inquiry from offseas investors, Hornery said.

"We probably won't be able to transact anything with them because there is no withholding tax exemption, but it's good to see that there is a large degree of publicity for the transaction worldwide," he added.

The domestic bond market has seen a rapid flow of debt issuance from non-government entities this month at over A$1.5 billion, which institutions are moping up in the absence of supply from the Australian Treasury and state governments.
ANZIB expects to bring another two or three debt issues to the market in the next three of fourth months.

ANZIB's Head of Origination Steve Davey comfirmed that the bank has recently been mandated to lead a A$250 million combined commercial paper and medium term note programme for BB plus rated Bonlac Foods.

"The non-sovereign sector is looking very good. It has had a lot of detractors initially on the question of pricing and liqiuidity. But it is adding a diversity of stock to the market and its really starting to generate a momentum of its own," Hornery said.

"It certainly hasn't matured to the level we think it will over the next year or two, but it is certainly improving substantially and generating the confidence of the funds managers increasingly," he added.
The Loy Yang consortium is led by U.S. utilities NRG Energy Inc and CMS Energy Corp, and also includes Macquarie Bank Ltd's Infrastructure Trust.
